questions.scenario: A massive sibling fight erupts over the TV remote during the IPL finale. How do you handle it?

options.text: Loudly argue your case, bring up past favors they owe you, and aggressively fight until they hand it over.
Check the exact TV timing rules mummy set yesterday to logically prove it is officially your turn.
Start a mini-protest about how elder/younger siblings always get an unfair advantage in this house.
Confiscate the remote, calm everyone down, and declare a fair 30-30 minute split between the two of you.

questions.scenario: During an intense game of Gully Cricket, a batsman claims they aren't out because 'one-tip-one-hand' doesn't apply to the boundary wall. Your reaction?

options.text: Get right in their face and debate fiercely until the opposing team backs down and accepts the wicket.
Analyze the exact rules everyone verbally agreed upon before the toss to point out the technicality.
Point out that the younger kids fielding at the boundary never get to bat, demanding a fairer game for all.
Listen to both sides yelling, quiet them down, and give the final, non-negotiable verdict: 'Out hai, chal nikal!'

questions.scenario: Someone steals your lunchbox (loaded with paneer parathas) during the PT period. What is your next move?

options.text: Directly confront the prime suspect in front of the whole class and demand a confession.
Investigate the scene, check who didn't bring lunch today, and piece together the logical clues.
Give an emotional speech in class about trust, sharing, and why stealing hurts the class unity.
Report the matter to the class monitor or teacher and suggest a fair way to check everyone's bags.

questions.scenario: You are at Sarojini Nagar or a local market with Mummy, and the shopkeeper asks for Rs. 1000 for a simple top. What do you do?

options.text: Actively haggle, counter-offer Rs. 200, and use the 'walk-away' tactic to aggressively get the best deal.
Quickly inspect the fabric, spot minor stitching defects, and use them as factual evidence to drop the price.
Feel a bit bad for the shopkeeper's hard work and convince Mummy to pay a fair, respectable middle price.
Let Mummy and the shopkeeper argue for a bit, then step in to decisively settle the deal at Rs. 500.

questions.scenario: Your tuition teacher catches your friend group passing chits during a boring Math lecture. How do you react?

options.text: Confidently debate with the teacher, arguing that you were just discussing a valid syllabus doubt.
Show your fully completed worksheet to prove you only passed the chit because you were already done.
Take the blame yourself so your best friend doesn't get a strict scolding from their strict parents.
Accept the mistake calmly on behalf of the group and promise it won't happen again, avoiding drama.

questions.scenario: You get your Unit Test answer sheet back and realize the teacher unfairly deducted half a mark. What’s your plan?

options.text: March straight to the teacher's desk and fiercely defend your answer until you get that half mark back.
Compare your sheet with the textbook and the topper's sheet to find the exact discrepancy in the marking scheme.
Gather all the students who lost marks on that confusing question and represent them to the teacher together.
Review the paper objectively, realize the teacher's logic actually makes sense, and peacefully move on.

questions.scenario: Your friend group is arguing over where to go for the 10th standard farewell treat. How do you contribute?

options.text: Strongly push for your favorite cafe and actively shoot down all other suggestions until they agree.
Create a mental (or literal) Excel sheet comparing the per-head cost, menu, and distance for 3 different spots.
Ensure the chosen place is affordable for everyone in the group and has good vegetarian options so no one feels left out.
Listen to everyone's chaotic shouting, cut through the noise, and make the final, balanced choice for the group.

questions.scenario: The school canteen bhaiya suddenly increases the price of a samosa from Rs. 15 to Rs. 20. Your reaction?

options.text: Lead a boycott and loudly tell all your classmates to stop buying from him until he drops the price.
Calculate the recent inflation in potato and cooking oil prices to see if his price hike is logically justified.
Start a petition asking the principal to subsidize canteen food because Rs. 20 is too much for students' pocket money.
Have a reasonable chat with the canteen bhaiya and suggest a 'Samosa + Frooti' combo deal to keep everyone happy.

questions.scenario: Papa scolds you for spending too much time on your phone instead of studying. How do you respond?

options.text: Rapid-fire argue back, fiercely listing all the times you were actually using YouTube to study Science.
Open your Digital Wellbeing/Screen Time stats to factually prove that educational apps took up 70% of the usage.
Point out the hypocrisy that adults also spend way too much time forwarding fake news on WhatsApp family groups.
Agree to a mutually acceptable 'no phones at the dinner table' rule to keep the peace in the house.

questions.scenario: During the school Annual Day drama practice, everything is falling apart and the teacher is furious. What's your role?

options.text: Vigorously defend your fellow actors when the teacher scolds the group, taking the situation head-on.
Read the script carefully to pinpoint exactly whose missed cue caused the entire scene to collapse.
Advocate for the shy student standing in the back who isn't getting any lines or stage time.
Organize the chaos, calm the teacher down, and assign clear stage directions to fix the mess.

Criminal_Lawyer.title: The Courtroom Gladiator (Criminal Lawyer / Litigator)
Criminal_Lawyer.primary_match_text: You are fearless, quick on your feet, and never back down from a debate. You have the aggressive energy needed to fight for your side and win!
Criminal_Lawyer.day_in_the_life: Arguing intensely in the courtroom, cross-examining tough witnesses, finding holes in the police investigation, and fiercely defending your client's freedom.
Criminal_Lawyer.alternative_match_text: If not law, your argumentative skills would make you a great Politician, Investigative Journalist, or PR Crisis Manager.
Criminal_Lawyer.roadmap: 11th/12th: Any stream (Humanities/Commerce preferred). Entrance: Crack CLAT, AILET, or LSAT-India. Degree: 5-year BA LLB or BBA LLB. Next Steps: Specialize in Criminal Law and practice under a senior trial lawyer in District or High Courts.

Corporate_Lawyer.title: The Detail Detective (Corporate Lawyer / Legal Researcher)
Corporate_Lawyer.primary_match_text: You love rules, logic, and finding the loopholes everyone else missed. You are highly analytical and rely on facts, not just emotions.
Corporate_Lawyer.day_in_the_life: Drafting multi-million rupee business contracts, advising huge tech startups, analyzing complex government policies, and sitting in swanky corporate offices.
Corporate_Lawyer.alternative_match_text: If not law, your analytical brain would excel in Chartered Accountancy (CA), Data Analytics, or Corporate Finance.
Corporate_Lawyer.roadmap: 11th/12th: Commerce with Math is a great fit, but any stream works. Entrance: Crack CLAT or MH-CET Law. Degree: 5-year BBA LLB or BCom LLB from a top National Law University (NLU). Next Steps: Intern at Tier-1 corporate law firms.

Human_Rights_Lawyer.title: The Voice of the People (Human Rights Activist Lawyer)
Human_Rights_Lawyer.primary_match_text: You have a powerful sense of justice, a big heart, and you always stand up for the underdog. You want to change the system for the better.
Human_Rights_Lawyer.day_in_the_life: Filing PILs (Public Interest Litigations) in the Supreme Court, working alongside NGOs, protecting the environment, and fighting for basic human rights.
Human_Rights_Lawyer.alternative_match_text: If not law, your empathy and drive would make you a fantastic Social Worker (MSW), NGO Founder, or Public Policy Expert.
Human_Rights_Lawyer.roadmap: 11th/12th: Humanities (Subjects like Sociology and Political Science are great). Entrance: Crack CLAT. Degree: 5-year BA LLB. Next Steps: Intern with the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) or top NGOs, and take up pro-bono cases.

Judge_Magistrate.title: The Wise Decision Maker (Judge / Legal Magistrate)
Judge_Magistrate.primary_match_text: You are level-headed, calm, and naturally good at resolving conflicts fairly. People trust you to listen to both sides and do the right thing.
Judge_Magistrate.day_in_the_life: Presiding over the courtroom, listening quietly to angry lawyers, interpreting the Constitution, and delivering fair, life-changing judgments.
Judge_Magistrate.alternative_match_text: If not law, your leadership and fairness would make you an excellent IAS Officer (Civil Services) or a top-tier Business Manager.
Judge_Magistrate.roadmap: 11th/12th: Any stream. Entrance: Crack CLAT or State-level law entrance. Degree: 5-year BA LLB or 3-year LLB. Next Steps: Clear the highly competitive State Judiciary Exams (PCS-J) to become a Civil Judge/Magistrate.
